items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the executive law, in relation to distribution of the state register; and to repeal certain provisions of the executive law relating thereto
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S1971

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the executive law, in relation to
distribution of the state register; and to repeal certain provisions
of the executive law relating thereto

PURPOSE:  This bill would reduce state expenditures by eliminating
requirements to provide free hard copies of the State Register to
entities that prefer to access the free online version.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1. Repeals paragraph (c) of subdivision 1 of § 148 of the
Executive Law, which requires the Department of State to write
annually to city, town and village clerks to advise them that they may
receive a copy of the weekly State Register upon written request of
the governing body.

Section 2. Amends subdivision 2 of § 148 of the Executive Law, and
adds a new subdivision 4-a, providing that (a) the requirement to
provide a free copy of the weekly Register to each state agency and
legislator may be dispensed with upon request of the recipient, and

(b) the authorization to charge a fee for the Register applies only to
the paper version -the statute is amended to explicitly recognize the
availability, at no cost, of an online version of the publication.

Section 3. Effective date.

EXISTING LAW:  Currently, the Department of State is required to
provide written notice to city, village and town clerks advising them
that they receive the weekly hardcopy Register upon written request of
the governing body, and is required to provide such copies to agencies
and legislators. Although there is no statutory provision requiring
it, the online version of the Register has been available without
charge since 2003.

JUSTIFICATION:  Executive Law § 102 contains requirements for free
distribution of the paper version of the weekly State Register
(listing rulemaking actions and other public notices) that predate the
creation of a free online version of the publication. Currently,
anyone can view the State Register without charge at:
http://www.dos.ny.gov/info/register.htm.

This bill will enable the Department to conserve state resources and
reduce paper waste by eliminating an annual mailing to city, town and
village clerks to advise them of how to request pacer copies of the
publication. Executive Law § 148(1)(a) will continue to allow them to
receive these copies upon written request, but they can be informed of
this in less costly ways. The bill will also save money and paper by
allowing discontinuance of print subscriptions at the request of
agencies or individual legislators.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:  2013-14: S3245/A2560 - Passed
Senate/Governmental Operations Committee 2011-12: S4818-A/A8164 -
Passed Senate/Governmental Operations Committee


FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:  To be determined; anticipated savings to the
state.

EFFECTIVE DATE:  This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Relates to the distribution of the state register; requires the department of state make available at no cost an online version of the weekly state register, quarterly index and any special issues as directed by statute or deemed appropriate by the secretary of state.
